newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds hope for new heights after restful session.
newsitem.headline: Bunds hope for new heights after restful session.

text.p: German Bund futures ended the week little changed, using Friday's quiet session as a period of consolidation.
But analysts said the outlook for the market was positive, with the Bund future set to head towards historical highs in the medium term.
"The market is looking extremely bullish," said David Sneddon, vice president of fixed income at CSFB in London.
By 1513 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was trading unchanged on the day at 102.42, having stretched up to plot a new contract high at 102.52 earlier.

CSFB's Sneddon said that after the break above key resistance at 101.99 earlier in the week, the September futures contract has completed a bullish pattern on weekly continuation charts and should continue to head higher over few months.
"The next major resistance is a band from 102.47 to 102.59, and we could see a pull back from there to around the 102.00 region," he said.
"But then we should see it going up to 103.10 and then on to the 104.04 highs in the next one to three months."
On the fundamental side, the domestic focus for the week ahead fall first on Tuesday with June unemployment data and then on the scheduled passing of the 1997 and 1998 budgets on Friday.
But analysts said neither of these were likely to unsettle the debt markets significantly.
The Bundesbank holds its regular council meeting on Thursday away from Frankfurt, and will hold a news conference afterwards, although this, again, is likely to have little impact on the market.
